**Singapore's equatorial climate and the onset of the Southwest Monsoon are the dominant drivers behind the market's concentration around 30–32°C highs for June 16.** Daily maximum temperatures in Singapore typically range 30–32°C during June due to consistent solar heating near the equator, high humidity, and trade-wind patterns, with the long-term June average high near 31°C. Official guidance from Singapore's Meteorological Service notes that the Southwest Monsoon, now established, favors maximum temperatures of 33–34°C on many days in the first half of June, occasionally reaching ~35°C under reduced cloud cover, while thundery showers can suppress peaks.

Recent observations and short-term forecasts reinforce this narrow band. Multiple models and outlooks for June 16 project a high near 31°C (roughly 88°F), consistent with the 37.5% market-implied probability for 31°C and the combined ~81% probability for 30–32°C. A brief cool spell with unusually low minima (~20°C) occurred around June 12 amid heavy rain, but this has not altered the broader warm, humid regime. Cloud cover, localized convection, and any shifts in monsoon flow remain the key variables that could nudge the daily peak slightly lower or higher within the favored range. 

Traders appear to be weighting the strong climatological and forecast consensus for a typical June day, with limited probability mass assigned to outliers given the short forecast horizon and stable atmospheric pattern.

**Forecast consensus from European and global models centers on a Warsaw high of 19–20 °C for June 16, 2026, producing the market’s tight split between those two outcomes.** 

Short-range guidance from sources such as the Met Office, BBC Weather, and timeanddate.com shows daytime maxima of 19–20 °C (66–68 °F) under partly cloudy skies with light showers or sprinkles and moderate westerly flow. These conditions limit solar heating and keep readings below the mid-June climatological average of ~22 °C. Recent model runs continue to cluster in this narrow range after a sharp cool-down following the early-June heat spike, with cloud cover and modest wind providing the main downward pressure on peak temperatures. Traders are therefore weighting the 19 °C and 20 °C bins most heavily while assigning only modest probability to 18 °C or 21 °C, reflecting the small but non-zero uncertainty from timing of any afternoon clearing or slight model spread in 2-meter temperature forecasts. Resolution will hinge on official station observations, with any late revision in the final ECMWF or GFS runs capable of shifting marginal probability between the two leading outcomes.

Minor differences among leading outcomes hinge on the precise arrival time and strength of the afternoon sea breeze versus any residual hot, dry air advection—variables that short-range models resolve only within a narrow range.
